repicado-medio: A medium layered cut (repicado) falling just past the shoulders, about 3 to 5 cm below the tops of the shoulders. Choppy, well-blended layers start at chin level and continue all around down to the ends, removing weight so the lengths move freely. The perimeter is softly textured and slightly uneven rather than blunt, with point-cut, piecey ends. Front pieces fall from the jawline and blend into the layers. Middle or soft side part, airy volume at the crown and through the mid-lengths. Natural, effortless, movable finish. Keep the natural hair texture.
camadas-medias: A medium-length layered cut falling to the collarbones, with long, soft layers that begin around the jawline and cascade down to a gently rounded perimeter. The layers are slide-cut and seamlessly blended, with no visible steps, giving smooth movement, natural bounce and soft fullness through the mid-lengths and ends. Front pieces start at the chin and blend into the length. Soft side part, smooth crown with gentle lift, ends softly separated and polished. Classic, elegant, easy-to-wear finish. Keep the natural hair texture.
corte-reto-medio: A blunt, one-length medium cut falling about 5 cm below the collarbones, just above the armpits, cut straight across in a clean, strong horizontal line with no layers at all. The ends are thick, full and dense all the way around, and the front and back are the same length. Middle part, the lengths falling naturally over the front of the shoulders, natural volume at the root, minimal styling for a healthy, polished, minimalist look with a crisp perimeter. Keep the natural hair texture.
corte-v-medio: A medium V-cut: the sides fall to the collarbones and the length gradually increases toward the back, where the perimeter meets in a soft V point at about armpit level, between the shoulder blades. Long, blended layers start at the chin in front and follow the V shape, keeping the ends light and tapered. Front pieces fall at the jawline and blend into the length. Middle part, natural volume at the crown, ends softly thinned and piecey. Keep the natural hair texture.
corte-borboleta-medio: A medium butterfly cut falling just below the collarbones: short, voluminous layers start at the cheekbones and around the crown, creating a shorter, wing-like top section that blends into longer layers through the back and ends. Long curtain-style front pieces part in the center and sweep outward along the cheekbones and jawline. Styled with a voluminous round-brush blow-dry: lifted crown, front layers flipped away from the center, bouncy feathered ends flicking outward. Airy, full-bodied, glamorous finish with soft separation strand by strand.
desfiado-medio: A medium razor-cut style (desfiado) falling just past the shoulders: the overall shape stays long and only lightly layered, but every end is thinned and feathered with a razor so the perimeter is soft, wispy and slightly see-through instead of blunt. The tapered, delicate ends separate into fine, airy points that move freely. Front pieces are softly feathered at the jawline. Middle or side part, smooth crown, flowing, weightless, lightly textured finish. Keep the natural hair texture.
shaggy-medio: A medium shag cut falling to the shoulders, with many choppy, razor-cut layers throughout: short, rounded layers at the crown create lift and fullness on top, and progressively longer, thinned layers blend down to wispy, piecey ends resting on the shoulders. Feathered front pieces start at the cheekbones. A soft, wispy fringe falls to the eyebrows and splits slightly in the center. Tousled, airy, lived-in finish with separated, textured strands. Keep the natural hair texture.
corte-u-medio: A medium U-cut: the length falls just below the collarbones, and the back perimeter is shaped into a smooth, rounded U curve that is slightly longer at the center back, around the tops of the shoulder blades. Soft, blended layers start at the chin and follow the curve, distributing weight evenly for gentle movement and fullness at the ends. Front pieces fall from the jawline. Middle or side part, natural crown volume, ends full and softly rounded rather than thin. Keep the natural hair texture.
camadas-medias-franja-cortina: A medium layered cut falling to the collarbones, paired with curtain bangs: a long fringe parted in the center falls in two soft arcs to cheekbone level and sweeps outward, blending seamlessly into front layers that continue from the cheekbones to the jawline and the collarbones. Soft, blended layers through the back keep the lengths light. Smooth crown with gentle lift, bangs and front layers blow-dried softly away from the center, ends lightly separated. Keep the natural hair texture.
escadinha-media: A medium cut with front step layers (escadinha): the back is kept at one length just below the collarbones with a clean, straight perimeter, while the front sections on both sides are cut in clearly visible, stair-step layers that start at the chin and descend in even steps past the jawline and the shoulders down to the full length. Each step is defined and separated. Middle part, the front steps styled softly outward and away from the center, smooth crown. Keep the natural hair texture.
wolf-cut-medio: A wolf cut falling just past the shoulders: heavy, choppy layering creates a short, very full, rounded crown and top section with chin-length layers, while the sides and back are left longer, thinner and wispier, tapering down to piecey ends, like a shag-mullet hybrid. Curtain bangs part in the center and fall to the cheekbones, blending into the short front layers. Styled tousled with strong crown volume, separated razor-textured pieces and an untamed, edgy finish. Keep the natural hair texture.
medio-liso-escovado: A medium cut falling just below the collarbones with soft, invisible long layers, styled perfectly straight with a sleek, salon-quality blow-dry and flat-iron finish: every strand smooth, aligned and glossy, with mirror-like shine, no frizz, no waves and no curls. Middle part, smooth crown with a little natural lift at the root, ends straight, polished and slightly tapered, the lengths moving together like a silky sheet. The sleek straight texture is applied evenly to all of the hair.
medio-ondas-soltas: A medium layered cut reaching the collarbones, styled in loose, undone beach waves: soft S-shaped waves begin around cheekbone level and run through the mid-lengths, with the last 2 to 3 cm of the ends left slightly straighter for a modern, effortless look. The waves alternate direction section by section, with natural separation, gentle volume and a soft, touchable, satin texture. Middle or side part, relaxed crown. The wavy texture is applied evenly to all of the hair.
mullet-feminino: A modern mullet: the top and crown are cut in short, choppy layers with lift, the front and sides are short and textured, ending around the cheekbones and the tops of the ears, while the back is left clearly longer, falling past the nape to the tops of the shoulders in wispy, tapered layers. The contrast between the short front and the long back is obvious. A short, piecey fringe falls to the eyebrows. Razor-textured, edgy, tousled finish. Keep the natural hair texture.
camadas-invisiveis-medio: A medium cut falling just below the collarbones with ghost layers: internal layers are cut hidden beneath the surface, removing bulk and adding movement, while the outer perimeter still looks almost one length with a soft, full, straight line. No visible steps or choppy pieces on top. The result is lighter, bouncier lengths with natural swing and soft, airy volume through the mid-lengths. Middle part, smooth crown, ends full but soft and lightly beveled. Keep the natural hair texture.
picotado-medio: A medium choppy cut (picotado) falling to the shoulders: the perimeter is deeply point-cut into a chunky, notched, uneven edge, with separated, piecey sections of different lengths, while the interior has only a few light layers. Front pieces are choppy at jaw level. Middle or side part, natural crown volume, textured, deliberately broken-up ends, and a modern, undone, slightly messy finish with clear piece-by-piece definition. Keep the natural hair texture.
medio-anos-90: A 1990s-style layered medium cut falling to the collarbones, with chunky front layers that start at the chin and the cheekbones and round, bouncy layers throughout. Styled with a big round-brush blowout: strong lift at the root and crown, the front layers flicked back and away from the center, the ends curved and bouncing with voluminous movement. Middle or slightly off-center part. Glossy, full, polished 90s supermodel blowout finish with smooth, defined strands.
medio-pontas-para-dentro: A medium cut falling to the collarbones with soft, rounded layers, styled with the ends curved smoothly inward (C-curl): every section is blow-dried and bent under with a round brush so the ends wrap inward toward the nape in a soft C shape. Rounded, tidy silhouette with gentle volume at the crown and sides, front pieces curving inward along the jawline. Side or middle part. Sleek, glossy, polished, elegant finish with neat, aligned strands.
medio-pontas-para-fora: A medium layered cut falling just above the collarbones, styled with the ends flipped outward: long layers start at the chin, and the ends of every section are blow-dried and flicked up and away in a playful outward curl all around the perimeter. Front pieces flip outward at jaw level. Middle part, smooth crown with soft lift, sleek and glossy through the lengths, bouncy flicked ends. Retro-modern, polished blowout finish.
kitty-cut: A kitty cut, a softer and shorter take on the wolf cut, falling between the shoulders and the collarbones: choppy, textured layers start at the cheekbones and add rounded volume at the crown, blending into a slightly shaggy, lob-like perimeter with ends flicked gently outward. Wispy curtain bangs part in the center and fall to the cheekbones. Less disconnected than a wolf cut, with a balanced, rounded silhouette. Tousled, piecey, lived-in finish with soft separation. Keep the natural hair texture.
corte-old-money: A polished old money medium cut falling about 5 cm below the collarbones, with long, subtle, invisible layers and a soft, slightly rounded perimeter. Styled in a healthy-looking blowout: smooth root lift at the crown, a soft side part, sleek and glossy mid-lengths, and the ends turned under in loose, soft bends with gentle bounce. Front pieces fall softly from the chin and roll back. Understated, impeccably groomed, expensive-looking finish with silky, aligned strands and natural shine.
medio-assimetrico: A deliberately asymmetrical medium cut: one side falls longer, to about armpit level, while the other side is cut noticeably shorter, at about the top of the shoulder, with the perimeter sloping diagonally across the back from the short side to the long side. Soft layers start at the chin. A deep side part sits on the shorter side, sweeping more hair toward the longer side. Smooth crown with lift at the part, softly textured ends. Bold, modern, intentional asymmetry. Keep the natural hair texture.
bombshell-medio: A medium bombshell cut falling just below the collarbones, with long, rounded layers starting at the chin to build maximum volume. Styled glamorous and big: strong root lift, a deep side part with the top swept over to one side, and large, loose barrel curls rolling through the mid-lengths and ends, brushed out into soft, voluminous waves. Front layers sweep away from the part. Full, bouncy, glossy, high-volume blowout finish with soft, defined strands.
feathered-medio: A feathered medium cut falling to the shoulders: soft, tapered layers are cut throughout, and the side layers, starting at the cheekbones, are blow-dried back and away from the center so they roll outward like wings. The crown has rounded, airy lift, and the thinned ends curve back for a winged, flowing silhouette. Middle part. Bouncy, light, glossy blowout finish with soft, separated, feather-like strands.
shullet: A shullet, a blend of shag and mullet: shaggy, choppy layers at the crown and top add rounded volume, the sides are cut shorter and feathered to around jaw level, and the back is left longer, falling to the shoulders in wispy, tapered pieces. The transition from the shorter front to the longer back is soft and blended rather than abrupt. A wispy, broken-up fringe falls to the eyebrows. Tousled, razor-textured, effortless finish with airy separation. Keep the natural hair texture.
octopus-cut-medio: A medium octopus cut: the top and crown are cut in short, rounded layers that form a full, dome-like upper section ending around the jawline, while the hair underneath is left much longer and thinned into wispy, tapered, tentacle-like pieces that fall to the collarbones. The contrast between the voluminous upper section and the long, thin, separated lower strands is clearly visible. Soft middle part with wispy front pieces. Textured, airy, piecey finish. Keep the natural hair texture.
hush-cut-medio: A Korean hush cut falling just below the shoulders: soft, feathery, wispy layers start at the chin and are thinned and slide-cut so the hair looks light, airy and almost see-through at the ends. Long, wispy front pieces fall from the cheekbones and blend into the layers, with a light, see-through fringe swept slightly to one side. Smooth, flat crown with gentle volume around the jawline, ends feathered and softly flicked. Delicate, weightless, effortless finish. Keep the natural hair texture.
repicado-anos-2000: A Y2K choppy medium cut falling to the shoulders: short, razored layers on the crown and top, chunky, piecey front layers starting at the chin, and thinned, separated ends. Styled flat-ironed straight with the ends flicked slightly outward and each chunky section clearly separated, early-2000s style. Zig-zag or side part, smooth crown with a little lift at the back. Sleek, piecey, defined finish with razor-sharp ends.
medio-lateral-raspada: A medium cut with a shaved side: one side of the head is clipped short above and behind the ear in a clean, close 3 to 6 mm shave, while the rest of the hair falls to the shoulders with soft layers. A deep side part sweeps all the longer hair over to the opposite side, leaving the shaved side clearly exposed. Smooth crown with lift at the part, lightly textured ends. Bold, edgy contrast between the shaved area and the long, flowing lengths. Keep the natural hair texture.
medio-efeito-molhado: A medium cut falling to the collarbones, styled in a wet look: the hair is slicked straight back from the hairline with a high-shine gel finish, lying close to the head at the roots and crown, then combed through so the lengths fall behind the shoulders in defined, damp-looking, separated strands. No volume at the crown and no loose pieces in front. Sleek, glossy, editorial finish that looks freshly wet strand by strand.
